title: Research: exact Toom-3 five-product profile screen
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Constructs and verifies the exact five-product Toom-3 factorization for multiplying degree-two polynomials. The verifier reconstructs the rational interpolation map and checks all nine input monomial pairs.

A hypothetical block replacing nine selected rank-one recursive products with five saves four rank-one units. On the pinned complex profile, 64 realized blocks would clear the task card's five-percent local-ceiling gate; 210 would move the complex-side transfer cap above 0.002. At 254 hypothetical blocks, the local complex-side ceiling is [0.002086688163384, 0.002086688163385], corresponding to a local κ cap near 0.002082342962972. The selected forward and backward traces each contain 254 disjoint groups of nine rank-one climbs eligible under the phase-local movement model from #1817.

These are screening results, not a selected-provider construction: no group is bound to Toom coefficient inputs or outputs, and copies, scratch, dirty-state restoration, precision and native hosting remain unpriced. A direct scalar schedule costs 19 additions and 13 rational scales per hypothetical block.

This PR records a useful partial result and a negative global result. Under the retained transfer, the unchanged bit provider caps overall κ at 0.001730427469824, so the Toom-3 complex-side screen alone cannot reach overall κ > 0.002. Selected κ remains 0.001672660197076918. No new κ or supplier claim is made.

## Task and overlap

Base: freshly fetched canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`. Task `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, **changed scope** to screen a five-product bilinear convolution factorization and its selected-profile effect.

The overlap refresh covered 676 open PRs and 2,578 Discussions with complete pagination. PR #3895 (head `2e969106d82a7e53ee3a22580653521b4876cc6b`) remains an open draft for a two-root E8 rank-16 decoder; it does not bind a Toom-3 convolution block. This screen also differs from the diagonal rank-16 batching in #1779 and dependency-window model in #1817, and extends the two-coefficient Karatsuba screen in Discussion #1987. These matches are not a novelty certificate. Exact inputs, source pins and the original task card are recorded in the package; no pending-PR source is required.

## Validation

On CPython 3.12, the registered normal and optimized package replays passed:

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-toom3-five-product-screen --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-toom3-five-product-screen
```

The replay checks the rational identity, all nine basis products, negative controls, selected-source pins and event schedule, exact profile-ceiling brackets and the unchanged bit-side cap. Publication-byte and source-history checks passed for commit `23bb4de61d629e3f103a65baa7882b34042ab10f`. No supplier cold replay, native compiler replay or Lean proof is claimed.

## Credit

Credit the selected #1094 provider lineage; Josie Elliston / PR #1817 for the dependency-window batching model; contributors to Discussion #1987 for the Karatsuba screen; Arham Tahir / PR #1779 for diagonal rank-16 batches; and contributors to PR #3895 for the two-root E8 decoder. Prepared by Gonzalo Mier with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0; no independent human review claimed.

## Open next questions

Bind one of the eligible nine-climb groups to exact paired Toom inputs and five outputs, then charge the full interface and arbitrary-dirty restoration. Separately, test whether the selected bit supplier can exceed the primitive threshold 1/499 required for overall κ > 0.002. Until those boundaries are discharged, do not extrapolate the event-window count into a many-block construction. See `TASK.json` for the exact next experiment and blockers.
